question: Image Caption and Observation
answer:
A group of students sit together in a dorm room, playing Werewolf and spending time with each other.

My third observation happened during a casual Werewolf game night in the dorm. In the image, several students are sitting around the room, and the red Werewolf cards are placed on the floor. Some students sit on chairs, while others sit on the floor or near the bed. The room looks informal and relaxed, which makes the moment feel real. No one is doing something very serious or formal. Everyone is simply spending time together, talking, guessing roles, and reacting to each other during the game.

question: Interpretation and Reading Connection
answer: This moment shows love as friendship, comfort, and everyday connection. It is different from the competition story because this moment is not about performance or winning. It is more about relaxing together and creating shared joy. Smith’s article explains that love often appears through small acts of kindness and repeated attention. A Werewolf game can be understood as a small bid for connection because it invites students to listen, respond, joke, and stay involved with each other. Catron’s idea also helps explain this scene because closeness can be created through shared experiences over time. In this game, students are not just playing; they are building trust by sharing laughter, conversation, and attention. This observation suggests that love at UCSB is not only found in serious moments of help. It also appears in ordinary dorm moments where students feel comfortable being themselves.
